entries.claim: Logistic regression models the log-odds as a linear function of the predictors, so ln(p/(1-p)) = beta0 + beta1 x1 + ... + betap xp and p = 1/(1+e^{-z})
entries.locator: James et al., An Introduction to Statistical Learning, Chapter 4
entries.notes: Definition of the logistic model and the sigmoid link

entries.claim: Exponentiating a logistic coefficient gives the odds ratio, so the coefficient is the change in log-odds per unit increase in the predictor
entries.notes: Standard coefficient interpretation for logistic regression

entries.claim: The ROC curve plots true positive rate against false positive rate across thresholds, and the area under it equals the probability that a random positive is scored above a random negative
Logistic regression can be biased in rare-events data, motivating attention to class imbalance and better metrics than accuracy
entries.notes: Motivates the imbalance discussion in section 05

entries.claim: Logistic regression parameters are estimated by maximum likelihood, not by ordinary least squares
The 0.73 probability, the coefficient/odds-ratio table, the AUC value of about 0.82, the 0.1 percent fraud rate and the 20-score demo data are constructed teaching numbers
entries.notes: Not taken from any real dataset

entries.claim: The linear-versus-sigmoid figure, the ROC sketch and the threshold trade-off figure are teaching diagrams prepared for this lesson
